standard_prerequisites.name: Flat closed immersions and the same-chapter characterisation of them, which links flatness of a closed immersion to the failure of its support to be closed under generalization
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Invoked twice, at proof lines 5085-5088 and again at 5144-5146
standard_prerequisites.use: Carries the implication from the module condition to the topological condition and closes the last step of the converse.

standard_prerequisites.name: Support of a finite type quasi-coherent module is closed, and the stalk at a point of a finite flat module over a local ring is free, as cited from the exterior-algebra and local-algebra chapters
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies the support, shows it is closed under generalization when the module is flat, and provides the local freeness used in the final Nakayama step.

standard_prerequisites.name: Exterior powers of a finite flat quasi-coherent module are again finite flat quasi-coherent, their supports are nested, and the fibre of the i-th exterior power at a point is the i-th exterior power of the fibre
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the open and closed decomposition of X indexed by the rank and identifies the rank at each point.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nakayama's lemma in the form that lifts a basis of the fibre to a surjection from a free module over an affine neighbourhood
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the local surjection O_U to the power r to F restricted to U whose injectivity is the last thing to be proved.

core_obligations: From (1) to (2): given a flat closed immersion i : Z to X, the pushforward of O_Z is quasi-coherent and flat, hence finite locally free by (1), so its support Z is open as well as closed; this identifies condition (2) through the same-chapter characterisation of flat closed immersions (proof lines 5085-5089).

From (2) to (1), first half: for a finite flat quasi-coherent F the support is closed, and for a specialization x to x' the stalk at the generization is the stalk at the specialization tensored with the local ring, so flatness forces the support to be closed under generalization; by (2) the support is therefore open and closed (proof lines 5091-5110).

Apply the same argument to all exterior powers, whose supports are nested, and decompose X as a disjoint union of open and closed subsets U_i such that the support of the i-th exterior power is the union of the U_j with j at least i; a point of U_r then has fibre of dimension exactly r (proof lines 5112-5130).

Conclude finite local freeness: by Nakayama choose an affine neighbourhood U of a point of U_r and r sections giving a surjection from a free module of rank r, observe that the r-th exterior power of F over U is a finite flat quasi-coherent module with support all of U generated by the exterior product of those sections, apply the same-chapter characterisation of flat closed immersions to force the defining ideal to vanish, and conclude that the surjection is also injective (proof lines 5130-5149).
proof_roadmap: The easy direction turns a flat closed immersion into a finite locally free pushforward of the structure sheaf, whose support is then open as well as closed (proof lines 5083-5089).

For the converse, reduce (1) to the topological condition by studying the support of F and of all its exterior powers, decomposing X by rank and finishing with a Nakayama-style local argument on the top exterior power (proof lines 5091-5149).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts an equivalence between a module-theoretic condition on a scheme, that every finite flat quasi-coherent module is finite locally free, and a topological condition, that every closed subset closed under generalizations is open (statement lines 5068-5077). The proof is substantial in its second half: it uses flat closed immersions to get the easy direction, then for the converse shows that the support of a finite flat module is closed under generalization, applies the same reasoning to every exterior power, uses the nestedness of those supports to decompose the scheme into open and closed pieces U_i indexed by the rank, and finally produces a local surjection from a free module of the correct rank and proves it injective by applying the flat-closed-immersion characterisation to the top exterior power (proof lines 5079-5151). It is H2: the argument is a genuine scheme-level construction rather than a citation, but its individual inputs are standard local algebra and the author explicitly says the scheme case simply repeats the affine algebra argument, so no independent research-level claim is made for it.
